rules.title: Exact source, plan, grammar, asset, timing, and capability lineage
rules.disposition: Compiler/continuity-validator territory (Codex-owned); recorded here as classified knowledge only.
rules.rationale: Broken lineage is a mechanical, evidence-bound authority failure, not a taste finding; the v1.1 ruling accepts this class as the only blocking kind.

rules.title: Legal timing and readable-action windows
rules.disposition: Timing-solver and read-window validation (Codex-owned); no editorial quota.
rules.rationale: Cutting before a required read window or inside an unsatisfied action envelope is a measurable mechanical failure.

rules.title: Continuity of geography, axis, screen direction, and subject lifecycle
rules.disposition: Continuity validation (Codex-owned); intentional jumps require declared transition logic.
rules.rationale: Unexplained axis/geography reversals, teleports, and lifecycle dropouts are causal failures the audience can verify, not taste.

rules.title: Prop ownership, attachment, scale, depth-plane, and position consistency
rules.disposition: Continuity validation (Codex-owned).
rules.rationale: Unexplained prop jumps are mechanical discontinuities in the asset/continuity envelope.

rules.title: Executed camera and transition behavior matches its labels
rules.disposition: Deterministic validation of rendered samples (Codex-owned).
rules.rationale: A camera or transition label that does not match what was rendered is an evidence-bound honesty failure; motivation itself stays editorial.

rules.title: Action, gait, contact, plant, catch, handoff, and causal-response continuity
rules.disposition: Continuity validation (Codex-owned).
rules.rationale: Cuts across gait discontinuity or unreadable contact/causal response are mechanical action-consistency failures.

rules.title: No known fake-preview or accidental whole-body pose-swap techniques
rules.disposition: Prohibited unless an approved future style capability explicitly legitimizes a variant.
rules.rationale: Accidental opacity-stacked whole-body crossfades were project-observed (frame audit at ~0:16/0:20) and are a renderer-honesty failure; the v1.1 ruling keeps them prohibited.

rules.title: Asset integrity and deterministic honest render output
rules.disposition: Renderer authority (Codex-owned).
rules.rationale: Output must be what the sealed plan produced; integrity and determinism are mechanical authority properties.

rules.title: No hidden planner fallback
rules.disposition: Planner authority (Codex-owned).
rules.rationale: Silent substitution of planner intent is an authority failure; fallback must be declared.

rules.title: Shot with no primary purpose, contradictory purposes, or an unsatisfiable envelope is rejected
rules.disposition: Plan validation (Codex-owned); multiple useful functions are not a reason to split.
rules.rationale: The v1.1 ruling narrows v1's 'exactly one job' to mechanical rejection cases only; the vocabulary itself stays planner knowledge (SC-011).

rules.title: Shot purpose vocabulary: establish, advance, feel, punctuate, bridge, payoff, with compatible secondaries
rules.disposition: Planner context; no quota.
rules.rationale: Purpose labeling is useful planning knowledge and the base for reason codes; it is not a blocking editorial rule.

rules.title: Coverage vocabulary: wide, medium, close-up, insert, two-shot, listener reaction, POV are choices, not a mandatory sequence
rules.disposition: Planner context; distribution judged separately as soft findings (SC-030).
rules.rationale: Purposeful coverage is an accepted principle from the roadmap and reference patterns; it is vocabulary, not sequence.

rules.title: Listener reaction is motivated by who is listening or affected, not by a role label
rules.disposition: Planner context; an accepted roadmap principle without quota status.
rules.rationale: Reaction coverage is an accepted editorial principle; its frequency is a soft finding, not a gate.

rules.title: Cut motivation vocabulary: cut on action when motion carries the eye; cut on stillness when the completed event is the point
rules.disposition: Planner context; a cut on a hold is not inherently defective.
rules.rationale: Motivated cuts are an accepted principle; only the mechanical failure modes are invariants (SC-002, SC-003, SC-006).

rules.title: Motivated camera vocabulary: push, pull, pan, track, orbit, locked; one primary intent per shot
rules.disposition: Planner context; compound moves allowed with a declared reason and rendered proof (SC-005 governs label honesty).
rules.rationale: Motivated camera is an accepted principle; the v1 'never stack' phrasing is superseded by declared-reason compound permission.

rules.title: Scene energy-shape vocabulary: flat-comic, sustained-tension, rising, falling, breather, button, bridge, reveal
rules.disposition: Planner context; scenes are not forced through one universal curve.
rules.rationale: Energy shaping is an accepted principle; the v1 single settle→build→peak→release curve is generalized, not quota.

rules.title: Pre-reveal hold is an available directing device, not a quota
rules.disposition: Planner context; duration resolved by approved audio, action phase, read windows, grammar, scene energy, and the timing solver.
rules.rationale: Reveal preparation is an accepted principle; its duration is not a fixed frame count (SC-025 records the numeric claim as hypothesis).

rules.title: Transition kinds are planning vocabulary and EditorialTargets priors
rules.disposition: Planner context; an identical-pose dissolve can be intentional — not universally banned. Mechanical transition failures live in SC-048.
rules.rationale: Transition grammar is accepted knowledge; the v1 universal dissolve ban is superseded by semantic exceptions.

rules.title: Reveal coverage palette scales with importance: micro, beat, major, set-piece
rules.disposition: Planner context; the hard failure is unreadable causality (SC-050), not missing palette steps (SC-029 stays hypothesis).
rules.rationale: Reveal preparation is an accepted principle; v1's fixed four-shot pattern becomes an importance-scaled palette.

rules.title: Rig capability knowledge: gaze leads motion, anticipation → action → contact/impact → settle, living holds, view-correct facing
rules.disposition: Capability request knowledge; style targets with intentional exceptions, not universal gates. Numeric micro-timing stays hypothesis (SC-037, SC-038).
rules.rationale: Performance follow-through is an accepted principle; overshoot is optional by action and style.

rules.title: Timing authority hierarchy: approved final audio → guide voice → estimated timing; the deterministic solver owns final frames
rules.disposition: Timing authority (Codex-owned); estimated timing never overrides an approved or guide basis.
rules.rationale: Audio-led timing is an accepted principle and an authority hierarchy, not an editorial preference; word-count estimates are the fallback, never the master.

rules.title: Cues the plan requests must be exactly synchronized; sound density itself is editorial
rules.disposition: Planner context; the system does not require an effect for every footfall, reveal, whoosh, or magical event.
rules.rationale: v1's cue-per-event density is superseded: synchronization is required for requested cues only.

rules.title: J-cut and L-cut audio bridges are available polish, not requirements
rules.disposition: Planner context for the audio lane when it lands.
rules.rationale: Established editorial technique; not a gate.

rules.title: Pre-reveal hold duration of 8–16 frames and the claimed threefold reveal improvement
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration after blind-pilot measurement; no planner quota.
rules.rationale: No measured source in this repository supports the exact frame range or the 3× claim; v1.1 lists it as explicitly non-normative.

rules.title: Shot-duration CV < 0.15 flagged as metronomic
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; may become a warning only with the recorded minimum sample and semantic exceptions.
rules.rationale: A universal CV threshold has no measured support here; v1.1 permits a future warning only for ≥8 resolved shots with variation opportunity and no montage/audio prescription.

rules.title: No unchanged visual idea longer than 4 seconds
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; change is defined semantically (performance, framing, blocking, gaze, prop state, camera, lighting/effect, or audio meaning).
rules.rationale: A universal four-second limit is explicitly non-normative in v1.1; a six-second locked close-up with excellent acting is not a static tableau.

rules.title: No identical gesture or pose repeated within 6 seconds; ≥6 distinct gesture programs per character
rules.disposition: The project-observed repeat (hand-to-ear listen twice in 6s) is regression evidence; the universal 6-second limit and six-mandatory-gestures requirement stay unvalidated hypotheses. Repetition is meaningful only when the same semantic program, phase structure, timing, and screen function recur visibly.
rules.rationale: The motivating observation is real project evidence, but it supports a warning-class finding, not universal numbers.

rules.title: No more than 2 consecutive same-sized shots without stated justification
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; three same-sized shots may warn unless justified, four or more may warn more strongly, always with semantic context.
rules.rationale: Streaks are graded findings per the classification ruling, never automatic rejection.

rules.title: Reveal beats must expand to at least 3 of the 4 pattern shots
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; coverage scales with reveal importance (SC-019).
rules.rationale: Three-of-four coverage is explicitly non-normative in v1.1; only unreadable causality is a hard failure (SC-050).

rules.title: Kids profile shot mix ≈ 25% wide / 40% medium / 25% close / 10% insert, ±10%
rules.disposition: Soft reference prior only; distribution not judged below 8 shots, informational at 8–11, and may warn at 12+ only when substantially outside an exact grammar-bound target without valid semantic justification. Any future target must bind grammar-profile, show-pack, reference-analysis, sample-size, confidence, and evaluation-window hashes.
rules.rationale: No measured source in this repository validates the exact percentages; kept as a prior, never a quota.

rules.title: Hard cuts are ≥80% of boundaries
rules.disposition: Planner context; transition mix is a graded finding, not a gate.
rules.rationale: Established default practice; the exact percentage is unmeasured and must not harden.

rules.title: Dissolve of 8–16 frames requires the subject to change pose or position across it
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; an identical-pose dissolve can be intentional. The banned mechanical case is a dissolve concealing an unsupported full-body pose substitution (SC-007, SC-048).
rules.rationale: The v1 universal pose-change requirement is softened by v1.1's semantic exceptions; the numeric range is unmeasured.

rules.title: Foreground-occlusion wipe locked to the occluder's motion, 6–10 frames
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; the mechanical failure is a wipe that never occludes (SC-048).
rules.rationale: The frame range is unmeasured; the concept is accepted vocabulary (SC-018).

rules.title: One motivated camera move per shot; never stack push and pan without a stated reason
rules.disposition: Superseded by v1.1: compound camera is allowed when every component is supported, a structured reason is declared, and validation confirms the rendered samples (SC-015, SC-005).
rules.rationale: Recorded as the v1 claim and its v1.1 resolution; not an active restriction.

rules.title: Pose or expression evolves every 1–2 seconds during holds
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; living-hold micro-motion is a style target with intentional exceptions (SC-020).
rules.rationale: The interval is unmeasured; the underlying living-hold principle stays a prior.

rules.title: Gaze leads the head by 2–4 frames and the head leads the body by 2–4 frames
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; gaze-lead itself is accepted rig knowledge (SC-020) without the numeric offsets.
rules.rationale: Exact frame offsets are unmeasured.

rules.title: Blinks every 2.5–4.5 seconds, never on a metronome
rules.disposition: Hold for calibration; blink cadence is a style target with intentional exceptions.
rules.rationale: The interval is unmeasured.

rules.title: No semi-transparent multi-pose smear frames; speed is conveyed by spacing and background streaks
rules.disposition: Accidental semi-transparent whole-body crossfades remain prohibited; an approved smear drawing style may become a valid future capability.
rules.rationale: Project-observed ghosting is regression evidence and v1.1 keeps the accidental variant prohibited while allowing an approved future style capability.

rules.title: 15 shots per 30 seconds as a coverage density
rules.sourceSection: v1 worked example; v1.1 §Illustrative high-energy treatment
rules.disposition: One illustrative high-energy treatment, never a target or scoring rubric. Example rows must be labelled essential, optional coverage, or alternate before reuse.
rules.rationale: The v1 table demonstrates applied vocabulary on one throwaway showcase; its shot count and timings are illustrative per v1.1.

rules.title: Blind-pilot scoring rubric: clarity/causality 25, composition/coverage 20, motivated cuts 20, pacing/holds 15, reactions/performance 10, variety 10
rules.disposition: Accepted evaluation contract for human blind review; authorizes no validator or hard gate inside product code, and must not reward matching a proposed shot list.
rules.rationale: Recorded as the accepted blind evaluation contract; calibration of numeric thresholds waits for blind-pilot results.

rules.title: Transition mechanical failures: label mismatch, never-occluding wipe, unexplained teleport, background swap during continuous action, lifecycle/position jump, dissolve concealing unsupported full-body pose substitution
rules.disposition: Continuity/renderer validation (Codex-owned).
rules.rationale: These are evidence-bound mechanical and authority failures, distinct from transition taste.

rules.title: Cut mechanical failures: before a required read window, between incompatible action phases, across gait discontinuity, before readable contact/causal response, across unexplained axis/geography reversal
rules.disposition: Continuity validation (Codex-owned); a cut on a hold is not inherently defective.
rules.rationale: Mechanical cut failures are measurable; motivation stays editorial (SC-014).

rules.title: Reveal hard failure: unreadable causality — the audience cannot identify what was noticed, who reacted, or what changed
rules.disposition: Continuity validation (Codex-owned); palette completeness itself stays a soft finding (SC-029).
rules.rationale: Causality readability is the only reveal-related blocking condition in the v1.1 ruling.

classificationNotes.numericClaims: Every inherited v1 numeric claim (8–16 frames, CV 0.15, four/six-second limits, gesture counts, reveal counts, shot counts, and percentage mixes) is hypothesis, planner-prior, or example-only. No measured source in this repository validates the exact numbers, and none was invented or upgraded.
classificationNotes.hardInvariantScope: Hard-invariant is reserved for evidence-bound mechanical/authority failures: exact lineage, timing/read envelopes, causal/continuity/geography/axis/lifecycle/prop/contact/gait/action consistency, capability/approval authority, asset integrity, honest executed camera/transition behavior, deterministic honest render output, and no hidden planner fallback.
classificationNotes.preservedPrinciples: Purposeful coverage, listener reaction, motivated cuts/camera, energy shaping, reveal preparation, performance follow-through, and audio-led timing are preserved as planner knowledge (planner-prior) without quotas.
classificationNotes.blindPilot: The blind-pilot rubric is recorded as an accepted human evaluation contract; it authorizes no validator or hard gate inside product code.
